sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of predicted default, accounting for about 28% of the model's importance, and risk rises strongly as utilization climbs toward the top of its range.
The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver, with risk rising from no delinquencies to one and then to two or more.

The two leading drivers interact strongly: the effect of utilization is much larger for applicants with two past delinquencies than for applicants with none, so high utilization is far more dangerous when the credit file already shows delinquencies.
Income and length of credit history have moderate-to-weak effects, with higher income and longer histories both associated with lower predicted risk.
The debt-to-income ratio has a weak effect, with risk generally rising for higher ratios.

Recent credit inquiries interact with credit history length: the effect of inquiries reverses direction depending on how long the history is, and the data do not settle how this reversal should be interpreted in isolation.
Feature_b, feature_a and age hardly matter to the model's predictions.
The data do not settle whether utilization's effect depends on feature_a, since that interaction's share of importance is too uncertain to rule out a small effect.

The number of past delinquencies has a strong effect on default risk; default risk increases with the number of past delinquencies.
Default risk jumps at the number of past delinquencies = 0.5.
Income has a moderate effect on default risk; default risk decreases with income.
The length of credit history has a moderate effect on default risk; default risk decreases with the length of credit history.
The debt-to-income ratio has a weak to moderate effect on default risk; default risk increases with the debt-to-income ratio.
The number of recent inquiries has at most a weak effect on default risk; default risk increases with the number of recent inquiries.
Feature b hardly matters for default risk.
Feature a hardly matters for default risk.
Age hardly matters for default risk.
The effect of credit utilization grows with the number of past delinquencies.
The effect of the number of past delinquencies reverses its sign as credit utilization changes.
The effect of the number of recent inquiries reverses its sign as the length of credit history changes.
